correctness.rationale: For incomparable supports, a shared reception must cover both supports or be contained in both; the least required radius is max(N(x,y),N(y,x)), attained by the union or intersection. For comparable supports the best shared reception splits the coordinate gap and has radius ceil(gap/2). Thus the d_u>=5 rule and radius-two disjointness agree, but the independent reproduction uses only the literal balls. Its increasing-label pairwise disjointness search exhausts the 128 words and finds 2976 edges and 1680 four-cliques; each has empty common-neighbor intersection, ruling out any larger family. Generating the S_7 times complement images of both given representatives exhausts the census in disjoint classes of sizes 1260 and 420; dividing 10080 gives stabilizers 8 and 24. Both directional-difference multisets and coverage totals 72 and 80 agree. The individual ball size independently equals 1+7+binom(weight,2)+binom(7-weight,2); maxima meet the compatibility constraints with exactly the stated profiles. value.rationale: This is the first two-error case of the cited short-length optimum family, with an exact equivalence question not settled by the known cardinality. Classifying all optima under the channel's natural coordinate and bit symmetries identifies precisely two choices up to equivalence. These differ structurally (a comparable pair occurs only in the smaller orbit) and cover different numbers of received words at the same code size. A researcher choosing or comparing extremal codebooks can use these distinctions; the value is not a replay of the known bound.
